## Summary

`local_max_concurrent_queries: 1` in `proxy/config.yaml` is legacy dead config: the router derives the local concurrency limit from `session_slot_pool_size` (currently 3) in `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()`, with the legacy key only as a backward-compat fallback defaulting to 1. An operator reading the config sees a concurrency limit of 1 that is never applied, which is misleading (the effective limit is 3 slots). Discovered during the local-model busy-time analysis (LP-0MSG97N2F0090TO9).

The config comment already acknowledges the derivation ("This value is now derived from session_slot_pool_size by default... preserved for explicit override only") — the ambiguity is that the key still exists and can silently override pool size if set.

## User Story

As an operator, I want exactly one config key to control local concurrency, so that I cannot be misled by a dead/misleading setting.

## Expected behaviour / outcomes

- `session_slot_pool_size` is the single, documented source of truth for local concurrency.
- The legacy `local_max_concurrent_queries` key and its fallback path in `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` are removed, OR (if removal is deemed too risky) the key is commented out with a clear deprecation note and the fallback path logs a warning when used.
- No behavioural change in normal operation (concurrency stays 3).

## Suggested approach

1. Remove `local_max_concurrent_queries: 1` from `proxy/config.yaml` and simplify the surrounding comment.
2. Update `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` to read only `session_slot_pool_size` (drop the legacy fallback), or keep the fallback but log a deprecation warning.
3. Run proxy tests; verify no config-validation tests reference the key (see also config-consistency validation LP-0MSCABA5K0010LW2).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No reference to `local_max_concurrent_queries` remains in config or code (or, if kept as fallback, it logs a deprecation warning and is commented out in config).
- [ ] Proxy test suite passes; concurrency behaviour unchanged (limit = `session_slot_pool_size` = 3).
- [ ] Config comment updated to state `session_slot_pool_size` is the single source of truth.
data.title: Remove dead local_max_concurrent_queries config; session_slot_pool_size is the single source of truth

# Bump local slot-exhaustion retry attempts 1 -> 2

## Problem statement

Recommendation from the 2026-08-11 proxy usage analysis (maximize local LLM utilization). `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts: 1` with `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_delay_seconds: 0.1` gives a single grace retry before a request falls back to the remote tier when the local probe reports 0 available slots. Its documented purpose is right-after-restart races where slot probes briefly report 0 available. Bumping to 2 retries catches the same race plus near-finished streams that free a slot within ~0.2s.

Expected effect is sub-1% of fallbacks (contention fallbacks are 839/1608 = 52%, but the large majority are genuinely long streams, not sub-200ms races — see the cheap-mode queue policy item for the real contention lever). Low risk: adds at most ~0.2s latency to the remote-fallback path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts` set to 2 (delay 0.1s unchanged).
2. Routing logic unchanged otherwise: still falls back to the next provider after the retries are exhausted.
3. Tests: right-after-restart probe race resolves to local on the second retry; persistent exhaustion still falls back after 2 retries; total added latency bounded (~0.2s + probe time).
4. Full test suite passes (quiet mode).
data.title: Bump local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts 1 -> 2 (grace retry on slot exhaustion)

data.description:
Goal: Explore the bursty-fan-out workload pattern (agent sessions firing parallel requests in bursts) and recommend whether the contention queue (cheap mode, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D) caps should be tuned — vs adding slots — to improve local utilization and cut remote fallback.

Context (from proxy usage analysis, report window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52):
- Fallback events are highly bursty: 95% of the 1293 fallbacks occur within 60s of a previous fallback (median inter-arrival 4s, p90 21s) — agent sessions fanning out parallel calls.
- 37 requests queued→dispatched local and 17 fell back after the queue caps (fallback_after_queue) in-window; 120 local_dispatch_denied (active=1/2 observed at denial, below the 3-slot capacity).
- The contention queue wakes on `local_active_queries` decrement and lease release; context bypasses are never queued. Adding slots shrinks per-slot context (slots-vs-context trade-off) and raises context-bypass volume, so it is NOT a free win (see report recommendations and LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM).
- Hypothesis to test: with bursty fan-out, queue depth/wait caps (contention_queue_max_wait_seconds, contention_queue_max_depth) may be the binding constraint, and tuning them (or making them mode-aware fast/cheap) may recover more local dispatch than raising slot counts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quantify the burst profile: distribution of concurrent local requests during bursts, queue depth observed, queue-wait durations, and how many fallbacks occurred while the contention queue was non-empty (where derivable from logs).
- Evaluate the expected gain of raising queue caps (wait/depth) vs raising slot counts: projected additional local dispatches saved per window, with the slots-vs-context trade-off factored in.
- Recommend concrete config changes (values for contention_queue_max_wait_seconds / contention_queue_max_depth, per-mode if warranted) with quantified expected impact and risks (latency added by queueing, remote fallback avoided).
- Recommendation recorded as a comment on this work item; create follow-up implementation item(s) if config changes are warranted.
data.title: Explore and recommend contention-queue tuning for bursty agent fan-out: queue caps vs more slots

# Log-based contention queue simulation harness

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO

## Goal

Build a reusable simulation script that replays proxy log dispatch events with configurable queue cap parameters to project additional local dispatches saved under different contention_queue configs.

## Approach

Log-based simulation (replay approach) — parse existing log files, reconstruct dispatch-event timelines, then replay with modified parameters. No config changes or live testing required. (Q2 answer: option A — simulation only.)

## Data sources

- Proxy log files: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (rotated, ~6h files), 90-day retention.
- **Analysis windows:** Pre-2026-08-28 log files (e.g. 2026-08-27, 2026-08-26, 2026-08-25, ...). Aug 28+ windows are EXCLUDED — known anomalous data (Q1 answer: option B — use days before 28-8).
- Key log events to parse:
  - `contention_queue_dispatch` — carries queued_duration, policy, depth
  - `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` — carries queued_duration
  - `status_request` — carries queue snapshot (depth, policy, queued_count, fallback_after_queue_count)
  - `local_dispatch_denied` — active slot count at denial time
  - `Fallback triggered` — fallback reason, timestamp

## Simulation logic

- Parse all cheap-mode dispatch events from the log files, reconstruct per-request arrival/occupancy timeline (2-slot cheap mode, session_slot_pool_size=2).
- Replay the same arrival pattern with configurable `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` and `contention_queue_max_depth`.
- For each simulated config, compute: dispatched, fallback_after_queue, total fallbacks, median/percentile queue wait.
- Default simulation (cap=60s wait, depth=4) must reproduce observed counts within tolerance to validate the model.

## Deliverable

Script under `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_simulation.py` (or equivalent location under `proxy/`), testable, with clear CLI interface — mirroring prior benchmark-tool conventions (compare_results.py / project_session_retention.py style).

## Constraints / knowns

- Cheap mode = 2 slots; queue caps: contention_queue_max_wait_seconds=60 (clamped [1, session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds=1800]), contention_queue_max_depth=4 (clamped [1, 16]).
- The queue only engages when policy=queue AND mode=cheap; fast mode (3 slots, policy=fallback) never queues — simulate cheap windows only.
- 2026-08-29 report-window figures cited in parent (37 queued→dispatched, 17 fallback_after_queue) are from the anomalous Aug-28/29 window and serve only as scale reference, not as the primary dataset.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Script parses log files and reconstructs dispatch events for any given time window with ≥95% event coverage across the four event types (dispatch, fallback_after_queue, status_request queue snapshot, local_dispatch_denied).
2. Simulation with default caps (60s wait, depth 4) reproduces the observed queued→dispatched and fallback_after_queue counts from the replayed cheap-mode windows within ±10% tolerance.
3. Output includes per-simulation summary: dispatched count, fallback_after_queue count, total fallbacks, median/percentile queue-wait duration.
4. Configurable via CLI args: `--max-wait-seconds`, `--max-depth`, `--log-files`, `--output`.
5. Test suite: unit tests for the core simulation engine (replay known synthetic inputs → verify expected outputs); full project suite passes.
data.title: T1: Log-based contention queue simulation harness

# Burst profile quantification (parent AC1)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1 (log-based simulation harness singleton)

## Goal

Quantify the bursty fan-out profile of cheap-mode traffic from pre-2026-08-28 windows: concurrent local request distribution during bursts, observed queue depth, queue-wait duration distribution, and how many fallbacks occurred while the contention queue was non-empty.

## Deliverables

- A markdown report section (or committed analysis doc under `proxy/benchmarks/` / `docs/dev/`) presenting all quantified AC1 metrics for the replayed cheap-mode windows.
- Any reusable extraction code lives in the T1 harness; this item consumes it.

## Metrics (per parent AC1)

1. **Concurrent local requests during bursts:** distribution of `local_active_queries` (reconstructed from status_request/local_dispatch_denied active counts and stream lifetimes) during cheap-mode burst windows; burst definition from inter-arrival analysis (parent cites 95% of fallbacks within 60s of a prior fallback; median inter-arrival 4s, p90 21s).
2. **Queue depth observed:** distribution of `contention_queue_depth` from status_request snapshots and contention_queue_dispatch lines (which carry depth at dispatch).
3. **Queue-wait durations:** distribution of `queued_duration` from contention_queue_dispatch (dispatched) and contention_queue_fallback_after_queue (fell back, typically = wait cap).
4. **Fallbacks while queue non-empty:** count of `Fallback triggered` (cheap-mode, non-context reasons) that co-occur with queue_depth > 0 (via nearest status_request snapshot within a small time delta), where derivable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All four AC1 sub-criteria (concurrent distribution, queue depth, queue-wait durations, fallbacks-while-queue-non-empty) are quantified from the replayed pre-Aug-28 cheap-mode windows and presented in the report.
2. Burst definition is stated explicitly (thresholds used, e.g. inter-arrival window / concurrency floor) and applied consistently.
3. Methodology is documented and reproducible (script + command documented, following the conventions of prior benchmark reports).
4. A comment is recorded on the parent work item LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO summarizing the burst-profile findings and citing the committed report path (if committed) or the raw script output path.
data.title: T2: Burst profile quantification

# Queue caps vs slots projected-gain analysis (parent AC2)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1 (simulation harness), T2 (burst profile)

## Goal

Evaluate the expected gain of raising contention queue caps (wait/depth) vs raising slot counts in cheap mode: projected additional local dispatches saved per window, with the slots-vs-context trade-off factored in.

## Approach

- **Queue-cap scenarios (via T1 simulation):** sweep `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (e.g. 120s, 180s, 300s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` (e.g. 8, 12, 16) over the replayed cheap-mode windows; record projected additional queued→dispatched saved, residual fallback_after_queue, and added queue-wait latency percentiles.
- **Slots scenarios:** model 2→3 (and consider 2→4) slots in cheap mode.
- **Slots-vs-context trade-off (Q3 answer: A — reuse prior findings):** reuse the established trade-off from LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F (more slots → smaller per-slot context → more `large_context_bypass`/`context_too_large` fallbacks). Do NOT run new benchmarks. **If reusing prior findings materially compromises the estimate, flag this prominently in the report** (notify-in-report requirement) and note the caveat in the recommendation.

## Deliverables

- Comparison table: for each scenario (queue-cap variants; slots variants), projected Δ local dispatches saved per cheap-mode window vs current config (2 slots, wait 60s, depth 4), with the context-bypass penalty stated.
- Explicit statement of which lever (queue caps or slots) has higher projected impact and why.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Queue-cap tuning projected gain quantified with concrete recommended candidate values (at least 2 wait values and 2 depth values evaluated).
2. "Add slots" projected gain quantified with the context-bypass penalty included (per-slot ctx shrink → bypass increase), sourced from prior findings (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F) with citations.
3. Headline comparison produced: which lever recovers more local dispatch, with numbers.
4. If prior benchmark findings were reused and materially affect the estimate, the report must state this caveat up front.
data.title: T3: Queue caps vs slots projected-gain analysis

# Recommendation + config change proposal (parent AC3/AC4)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1, T2, T3

## Goal

Record a concrete, quantified recommendation on this work item and create follow-up implementation item(s) if config changes are warranted.

## Deliverables

1. **Recommendation comment** on LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO covering:
   - Whether to tune `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_depth` (and to which values), per-mode if warranted (fast mode currently policy=fallback — no change there unless analysis supports otherwise).
   - Or whether adding slots in cheap mode is the better lever (with the slots-vs-context penalty).
   - Quantified expected impact (additional local dispatches saved per window) and risks (added queueing latency, user-visible stalls if wait cap raised, depth-cap clamp [1,16] limits, interplay with `llama_adaptive_timeout_*` budget subtraction for queued waits).
   - Data sources cited (T1/T2/T3 artifacts; prior LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM findings where reused).
   - Assumptions + unknowns recorded (OPEN QUESTION entries where appropriate; e.g. whether live validation is needed before rollout).
2. **Follow-up implementation item(s)** created via `wl create` when config changes are warranted, containing the concrete diff (config-cheap.yaml values) and rollout notes. Read-only task if the recommendation is no-change.
3. If the recommendation is a no-go for cheap mode but the analysis surfaced fast-mode or global opportunities, note them as discovered-from follow-ups.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Recommendation comment recorded on LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO with concrete config values (or explicit no-change decision), quantified impact, and quantified risks.
2. Follow-up implementation work item(s) created (via wl) if and only if config changes are warranted, with the concrete change and rollout plan; the item references this work item (discovered-from/related-to).
3. Recommendation honors config clamps (wait ≤ session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds; depth ∈ [1,16]) and the fast-mode no-queue invariant.
4. Any assumption that materially affects the recommendation is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION entry in the parent.
data.title: T4: Recommendation + config change proposal
